Pin the object by its exact title (plus the submission id from the POST /submit 302 redirect) so the delete is provably scoped to the object you created. No content capture is needed — creation-only mutation with a native inverse and no prior state to restore. Delete is permanent (Postmill has no undo/restore for submissions) ; child-comment cascade is NOT verified, so only use this while the submission still has zero dependants; a self-delete by the author/owner leaves no Trash or mod-log entry.
LIMITATIONS: Untested: URL and image submission types; deleting another user's submission; moderator 'remove' (Actions) vs author Delete. Untested: reverting a submission that already has comments — child-dependent deletion is untested and Trash stayed empty, so cascaded comments would be unrecoverable; no child objects were created. Untested: title-collision / pagination when locating by title (forum had only 2 posts). Postmill has no revision/undo for submissions; delete is permanent, no restore attempted. Browser-only access; no shell/DB verification.

Postmill has no revision history, diff or revert for submissions, so capture the pre-state yourself or the original content is unrecoverable. Before saving, goto /f/<forum>/<id>/-/edit (note: /f/<forum>/<id>/edit does NOT 404 — it renders the submission page and a naive capture there silently reads nothing) and read the raw .value of #submission_title, #submission_body and #submission_url via browser_run_code_unsafe, never the rendered HTML, so the markdown source survives; the edit form has no forum select, so forum needs no capture. To restore, re-open the same /-/edit URL, fill the captured values verbatim, click 'Edit submission', then re-read the form and the rendered title/body and compare byte-for-byte. Recovery is content-complete but metadata-incomplete: the byline's '(edited N minutes later)' marker and edit timestamp appear on the first edit and survive the restore. A title change rewrites the canonical slug, so saved slug URLs break until the title is restored (the numeric-id URL keeps working).
LIMITATIONS: Postmill exposes no revision history, diff or revert for submissions — recovery is only possible from an externally captured pre-state; without a capture the original content is unrecoverable. patterns.test_case: Fixture: top-level comment patternfresh_20260911_comment_a (id 1754) on submission 742 in forum patternfresh_20260911_fx, with one child reply (id 1755) by the same author; dependants = the child reply, which is orphaned under a '[deleted]' tombstone and vanishes from the thread view; original op = author's own Delete (delete_own) on 1754; recovery = capture raw markdown + author/timestamp/permalink/parent/descendants before the delete, then re-post the captured body at the same parent and replay children depth-first, comparing raw bodies and nesting depth and reporting new ids/permalinks and lost original timestamps.
patterns.skill:
VERIFIED SCOPE ONLY: One Postmill comment with exactly one direct child, same author, single forum/submission, delete performed by the comment's own author via 'delete_own'. Untested: moderator delete of another user's comment, deeper/multi-page subtrees, comments with votes/flags/edited markers, deletion of a whole submission, Postmill-side purge of the tombstone, and any other application (ownCloud, GitLab) — none touched in this run.
Postmill has no undelete, revision history, Trash entry or moderation-log entry for comments, so recovery is capture-and-replay, not restoration. Before the delete, read each comment's raw markdown from its /-/comment/<CID>/edit textarea (it becomes 403 after deletion) together with author, timestamp, permalink, parent, and every descendant's raw body depth-first. To restore, POST the captured body as a new comment at the captured parent (submission-level form for a top-level comment; per-comment form for a nested one, which only exists in the DOM after clicking that comment's 'Reply' link), then replay each captured child under the newly issued parent id. Verify by reading the new comments' edit textareas back and comparing byte-for-byte against the capture plus scanning rendered nesting depth. Expect new ids/permalinks and new creation timestamps, and expect the original tombstone plus its orphaned children to remain in the database and in the thread counter — the restore duplicates the subtree rather than replacing it.
LIMITATIONS: Postmill offers no undelete, revision history, Trash entry or moderation-log entry for comments, so recovery is re-creation, not restoration. Recovery is partial by construction: new comment ids and permalinks are issued and the original creation timestamps are permanently lost; only body text, author (when the restorer is the original author), and nesting shape are reproducible. The delete leaves a permanent '[deleted]' tombstone plus the original orphaned child (1755) in the database — hidden from the thread view but live at its permalink and still counted by the '3 comments' counter; the UI offers no way to purge it, so restore duplicates the subtree rather than replacing it. Child replies cannot be re-parented, so surviving children must be replayed as new comments under the restored parent. The per-comment reply form (and its CSRF token) exists in the DOM only after clicking that comment's 'Reply' link; there is no GET-able /reply page (returned 404). Only browser/HTTP access was available (no DB or shell), so persistence beyond the rendered pages was not inspected.

patterns.skill:
VERIFIED SCOPE ONLY: One small text file on one ownCloud account via WebDAV PUT with Basic auth. Content + checksum + size recovery only, on an unshared, untagged, unfavourited file.
Overwrite is not self-inverting: ownCloud keeps no recoverable handle to the previous bytes through the write itself, so capture before the write. GET the full bytes from /remote.php/dav/files/<user>/<path> with Basic auth and stream them to an artifact file (never hold them only in context), and record PROPFIND Depth:0 metadata (getcontentlength, getetag, getlastmodified, oc:checksums, oc:fileid) plus the OCS share list for the path. Restore by PUTting the captured bytes back to the identical path, then re-GET and re-PROPFIND and compare raw body, size and SHA1/MD5 against the capture. Content, size and checksums recover exactly; ETag and mtime do not, and each PUT (mutation and restore) appends a version entry under /remote.php/dav/meta/<fileid>/v that cannot be pruned — report both as residue. A native version-rollback inverse exists (COPY from the meta versions collection) but was not exercised here.
LIMITATIONS: ETag and last-modified are not restorable — any consumer keyed on ETag/mtime sees a changed resource. Version history grows monotonically; the overwrite and the restore each add a version entry and none can be pruned through the tested surface. Native version-rollback inverse (COPY /remote.php/dav/meta/<fileid>/v/<ts> onto the live path, or the versions UI) was observed to exist (207 listing with prior revisions) but was NOT executed. Shares, favourites and tags were not exercised: the fixture had no share (OCS data []), no tag, no favourite, so preservation of those dependants across an overwrite is untested. Only a 59-byte file was used; chunked/large-file upload and browser_file_upload UI path (the pattern's applies_to) were not exercised — verification used the equivalent WebDAV PUT the upload performs. Playwright script sandbox lacks the Buffer global (Buffer.from threw); base64 decoding of the capture had to happen outside the sandbox, so a true binary restore needs the bytes re-encoded on the agent side or a file-backed PUT.

VERIFIED SCOPE ONLY: One live example only: Postmill image-submission upload of a single 92-byte new PNG into one fixture forum, recovered by the native submission Delete. Untested scope: the overwrite branch of the pattern (same-named file existing -> capture bytes and write them back) was NOT exercised anywhere; ownCloud UI upload and its versions/trash-restore semantics were not verified (UI upload is broken there, see limitations); GitLab issue/MR attachment upload was not attempted at all; multi-file uploads, large/chunked uploads, share-state or version-history dependants, and upload into shared (non-fixture) destinations were not tested.
Creation-only upload: before uploading, GET the destination listing and record the entry names. After the upload, record the created object URL and the server-side blob URL. Recover by deleting exactly the created object through the app's native Delete (accepting its confirm dialog) — in Postmill the blob's lifetime is coupled to the submission, so the blob 404s too. Then re-GET the object, the blob, the listing, the trash view and the moderation log and diff the listing against the capture. If a same-named file already exists at the destination, this is an overwrite, not a creation — that branch requires capturing the prior bytes first and was not exercised here.
LIMITATIONS: ownCloud 10.0.10.4 (http://the-agent-company.com/) browser upload is non-functional on this instance: #file_upload_start is hidden, the '+ New' toolbar container stays 'actions creatable hidden', and the Files app JS loops PROPFIND /remote.php/webdav/<dir> -> 401 Unauthorized, causing periodic self-reload. After force-unhiding the input, browser_click DID open the chooser and browser_file_upload setFiles succeeded, but no PUT was sent — the folder PROPFIND stayed empty and GET of the file returned 404. So browser_file_upload could not be verified on ownCloud; the ownCloud arm of the pattern is unavailable via the UI (WebDAV PUT remains a programmatic alternative, untested here). ownCloud 10.0.10 has no trashbin DAV endpoint (PROPFIND /remote.php/dav/trashbin/theagentcompany/trash -> 404); purging a tombstone requires POST /index.php/apps/files_trashbin/ajax/delete.php with the page 'requesttoken' header and the trash name including its '.d<timestamp>' suffix. That endpoint returns status:success even for names that are not real trash entries, so a purge response is not evidence of deletion — re-list the Deleted files view to confirm (verified: three earlier-run live root files named in a bad-name purge attempt were confirmed still present). Postmill rejects some valid PNGs ('The image file is corrupted.' for an 8x8 1-bit grayscale PNG); a 16x16 8-bit RGB PNG was accepted. Payload format constrains this upload op. Postmill's file input and the media-type radio are CSS-hidden, so browser_click on them times out; the chooser must be opened by clicking the radio's <label> first and then clicking the (now visible) file input with noWaitAfter — an extra browser_run_code_unsafe step before browser_file_upload. Recovery here relies on Postmill coupling blob lifetime to the submission (deleting the submission 404s the blob); this content-addressed blob is not separately addressable/deletable via the UI, so an app that keeps orphan blobs after object deletion would need a different inverse. Not generalizable beyond this app from one example. The uploaded blob's identity was matched by byte length (92) and PNG header only — the Playwright sandbox has no Buffer/btoa/crypto and no require, so no server-side checksum was computed; the ownCloud OCS-advertised SHA1 checksum path was not used.

skill:
Backup guidance for browser services. Match application AND operation; use current instance URLs and stable IDs. Before mutation, save actual fields/bytes and affected dependents, with pagination. DOM snapshots or re-navigation do not undo server writes. Creation inverses target only new objects without later dependents. Capture now; do not execute the main destructive action. Verify restored content/state; IDs, timestamps and audit history may differ. Unmatched actions use generic backup guidance.

[1] Postmill create submission: pin new ID/permalink/title. For an own text post without dependents, Delete + confirm reverses creation; verify absence and prior listing. Other authors/types or existing comments are outside this scope.
[2] Postmill create comment: pin ID, parent and author. Delete_own + confirm reverses a new own top-level comment without replies; verify parent unchanged. Child-cascade recovery is unproven.
[3] Postmill create forum: pin new name and prior absence. Reverse at /f/<name>/delete with name confirmation only while empty. Existing posts/subscribers/dependents are excluded.
[4] Postmill edit submission: save raw title/body/url and identity/dependents from the edit form. Restore through that form and compare values. Content/slug can return; edit timestamp/byline residue remains.
[5] Postmill edit comment: save raw markdown, identity and child relations; restore through the edit form and compare. Edit metadata remains; rendered HTML alone is insufficient.
[6] Postmill delete comment: capture raw parent/child bodies, authors and nesting before delete. No native Trash restore was found; recreate captured comments in dependency order. Content/nesting can return with new IDs/times and tombstone/count residue; not identity-preserving recovery.
[7] Postmill edit forum: capture and restore /edit text settings. Tested title/description/sidebar/tags on an empty forum; appearance, slug rename and dependent content are excluded.
[8] Postmill biography: capture raw text, restore through edit_biography and compare profile/form. Preferences toggles were never mutated; this does not verify general account-setting recovery.
[9] Postmill vote: pin target and prior vote; restore through matching vote/retract controls. Tested submission up -> none -> up only, not comment or opposite-vote transitions.
[10] Postmill subscribe: pin forum and prior subscription; restore the toggle and compare subscribed listings. One account/forum only; notification settings are excluded.
[11] Postmill moderation: capture forum-scoped ban state and exact target, then restore that prior ban state with native controls. Only a disposable forum ban/unban was tested; trash restore, global bans, timed bans and moderator recovery are not established.
[12] ownCloud overwrite: GET the old file bytes and PROPFIND its identity/metadata before PUT. Persist and hash the bytes; restore by PUT and compare content/size. ETag, mtime, versions, shares and tags are not recovered merely by restoring content.
[13] ownCloud delete file/folder: recursively capture all descendant bytes, relative paths and metadata before DELETE. Recreate hierarchy with MKCOL/PUT and compare each file. Recreated identities and untested shares/tags/history remain limitations.
[14] ownCloud purge trash: download actual bytes and record original paths/metadata before permanent removal. Restore with MKCOL/PUT as needed and compare checksums. Recreated files do not preserve trash identity, timestamps or version history; a bin listing is insufficient.
[15] ownCloud share change: capture the complete share record and permissions before PUT, then restore captured values. For new public links, pin and revoke only that new share. Re-created secrets/tokens differ; expiry and undisclosed passwords are not proven recoverable.
[16] ownCloud MOVE/rename: pin source path, destination absence, file ID and dependent share bindings. Invert with MOVE to the saved source path and verify identity/content/share. Tested scope is a same-owner file move with one link share, not overwriting a destination.
[17] ownCloud create folder: pin new path and prior absence. DELETE reverses MKCOL only without subsequent content/dependents; verify absence. Existing folders and file overwrites are excluded.
[18] ownCloud favourite/tag: capture exact prior favourite flag and tag set plus file ID with WebDAV properties. Restore those properties and compare. Tested one-tag scope does not establish ordering, system-tag or every UI variant behavior.
[19] GitLab create project: pin new numeric ID and prior absence; delete that exact project only before later work/dependents accrue. Pre-existing or populated projects are excluded.
[20] GitLab create issue: pin project ID and new iid; delete that issue and verify absence. Tested a minimal issue without notes/attachments; populated issues need capture first.
[21] GitLab edit issue: capture title/description/labels/assignees/milestone/state and affected notes via API. PUT captured fields and reopen if required, then compare. System notes, timestamps and other audit residue may remain; a 200 response alone is not verification.
[22] GitLab edit/delete note: capture raw note body, author and discussion/reply links before mutation. PUT restores an edit; re-post restores deleted content with new identity/time. System notes, MR diff positions and untested discussions need separate handling.
[23] GitLab delete branch: capture exact SHA, branch-only commit content, protection and dependent MR state. Recreate the branch at that SHA, reapply protection and reopen affected MRs; verify all three. This does not prove recovery after unreachable commits are garbage-collected.
[24] GitLab delete project: request/download a completed project export BEFORE deletion and inspect its contents for required state. Import and verify branches/commits/issues/notes/wiki. Project identity changes; variables, integrations, LFS and other excluded/untested resources need separate capture.
[25] GitLab visibility/settings: capture visibility and all feature access levels plus relevant membership/protection records. Restore via API PUT with captured values and compare. Restoring visibility through the UI alone can silently clamp other feature permissions.
[26] GitLab snippet: capture metadata and actual raw file content. PUT restores an edit on the same ID; POST recreates a deleted personal snippet with new ID/URL/time. Tested single-file personal snippets do not cover project snippets or repository history.
[27] GitLab create token: pin the newly created token's ID/scopes/expiry and prior token inventory. Revoke only that token to reverse creation. A revoked pre-existing token's secret and its consumers cannot be restored from the visible token list.
[28] Scripted request: inspect the actual target and HTTP operation. Tested ownCloud PUT requires pre-GET bytes plus PROPFIND metadata, then restore with PUT and compare. Do not run fixture setup or the destructive request during backup; other APIs need their own capture.
[29] Submit form: capture durable raw values of every affected control and server object before submission. Restore captured values through the same form and verify server state. Tested Postmill text/URL controls retain edit residue; passwords/files and other sites are not established.
[30] Type with submit: distinguish unsaved input from persisted server state. For the tested ownCloud folder rename, capture old name/path/ID, invert the rename and verify old path present/new absent. New-object deletion applies only to confirmed creations without dependents.
[31] Upload: distinguish new upload from overwrite. For the tested new Postmill image submission, pin both submission and blob and reverse via submission Delete; verify both absent. ownCloud upload and existing-file overwrite were not verified; capture prior bytes before overwrites.
